comment: ‘Non-transactional’ is not a defensible defining property of shared infrastructure. Registries, benefits registries, supply services and surveillance platforms perform transactions and state-changing workflows, even at clinical level. The criterion also conflicts with the document’s own business-service components and could cause inconsistent conformance decisions.

reviewer.name: Brian O'Donnell (on behalf of HISP-UiO)
reviewer.organisation: HISP Centre at University of Oslo

public.text: ‘Non-transactional’ is not a defensible defining property of shared infrastructure. Registries, benefits registries, supply services and surveillance platforms perform transactions and state-changing workflows, even at clinical level. The criterion also conflicts with the document’s own business-service components and could cause inconsistent conformance decisions.
public.suggestedRevision: Delete the ‘non-transactional’ criterion. If the intended concern is excessive coupling to one application, say: ‘not tightly coupled to a single programme or point-of-service workflow, and usable through stable interfaces by multiple authorized services’.
